accepted: Stationary ALIGN remains a fail-closed stop-turn-go fallback; continuous curvature is a distinct mode that requires explicit swept-arc evidence and independent braking, lateral, yaw and wheel limits.
Synthetic orthogonal maze fixtures, deterministic seeds, role-paired evaluation, and hard safety exclusions are useful software preparation.
qualified_or_rejected: A dense 360-degree scan and radial clearance bound only the declared SIL geometry and bounded error model; they do not prove physical swept-volume safety, arbitrary-obstacle detection, dynamic-obstacle safety, or actuator response.
Fixture parameter values are not robot calibration and fixture episodes are not eligible evidence for G4, G5, or policy promotion.

Explorer movement and scan-residual opponent tracks now exist only inside a synthetic SIL fixture; they are not validated competition behavior or perception, so empirical evolutionary claims remain unauthorized.
Held-out data must remain unused until a separately controlled, once-only final evaluation procedure is implemented.

features: Immutable versioned tactical genome over registered role-specific utility features, bounded signs and coefficient mass, hysteresis, and dwell.
Deterministic seeded projected Gaussian mutation within declared genome bounds.

Role-swapped candidate-vs-fixed-baseline matches paired by scenario, seed, map, opponent, seed bank, and role; candidate Guardian and Explorer policies are assessed in separate matches against the corresponding baseline opponent.
Legacy candidate-self-play versus baseline-self-play runner remains available for fixture comparison but is not used for evolutionary fitness because zero-sum role deltas cancel by construction.
Hard candidate exclusion for incomplete episodes, collision, safety violation, excess safety overrides, or increased overrides relative to baseline.
A separate simultaneous two-role SIL fixture with role-scoped stages, synthetic scan-residual tracks, fixture-only Guardian pursuit and Explorer navigation, and safety-certified curved motion.

Deterministic single and paired episode runner instantiates the two role policies from TacticalGenome, runs paired worlds with identical scenario/seed/sensor seeds, and returns role-specific EpisodeResult records with configuration provenance.

Terminal-only zero-sum capture/timeout surrogate discounted by exp(-beta * active_duration); capture terminalization is restricted to straight-command intervals to respect the piecewise-linear referee motion model.
Episode outputs are explicitly labeled SIL_DEVELOPMENT_FIXTURE_NOT_PROMOTION_ELIGIBLE, have no official score, and the runner rejects the reserved held-out split.
Evaluation pair identity includes an evaluation-profile hash over runner configuration and fixture geometry to reject mismatched baseline/candidate runs.
Paired Student-t confidence interval and per-role deltas; official score is explicitly unavailable.
Training-only fitness ranking, bounded deterministic next-generation creation, and validation-only selection with baseline retention absent supported non-regressing improvement.

Explicit development-fixture population orchestrator evaluates candidate generations on training maps, selects one train finalist, validates it once at 95% two-sided Student-t confidence, and labels all outputs non-promotable.
Policy artifact loader verifies the tactical genome hash and rejects missing or altered fixture-only authority labels.
Post-search self-play demo consumes the serialized policy and exports trajectory/command/option telemetry as JSON and SVG without an added plotting dependency.

Larger maze topologies can produce more than 32 tactical proposals; the policy now uses the existing core maximum bound of 256, avoiding a fixture-scale proposal-count crash without changing the global selector limit.
Genome weights can be wired into role-specific SIL utility profiles without modifying safety predicates, action realizers, or physical authority.
not_implemented: Accepted deterministic G4 baseline or eligible empirical P6.3 optimization and dataset.
Accepted competition-grade Explorer policy or validated real-world opponent detection/tracking/belief.
Once-only held-out evaluation with an immutable use ledger.
Shadow logging, promotion review, or G5 acceptance.

development_tools.search_boundary: Requires --development-fixtures in CLI; results cannot be promoted and no held-out episodes are executed or scored.
development_tools.fitness_protocol: Candidate Guardian vs baseline Explorer and baseline Guardian vs candidate Explorer, each paired role-wise against baseline-vs-baseline runs.
development_tools.validation_protocol: Select one training finalist and evaluate it once on validation with 95% two-sided Student-t interval; baseline retained otherwise.
development_tools.visualization: Standard-library SVG plus JSON trajectory, commands, chosen options, per-role safety metrics, and hashed scenario/evaluation provenance; no additional dependency.
development_tools.statistical_limitations: Four training maps and two validation maps are synthetic fixtures; the validation interval has only two paired map-level observations and is diagnostic, not generalizable evidence.

constraints: Map, opponent, and seed-bank assignments are split-disjoint.
Fixtures are finite connected orthogonal grids converted to versioned topology and wall geometry; all open cells must belong to the connected component.
Two 7x7 training maps and one 7x7 validation map increase synthetic scale/topology diversity without claiming competition-course representativeness.
Synthetic goal is explicitly unauthorized as a competition objective.
Loader rejects truth/authority claims, leakage, malformed grids, disconnected routes, and invalid seeds.

motion_prerequisite.description: The optional simultaneous-duel SIL profile supports straight translation, full-scan-certified constant-curvature translation under declared fixture bounds, and fail-closed stationary ALIGN. It includes scan-residual opponent tracks and fixture-scoped Guardian/Explorer behavior. Arc/ALIGN checks subtract declared geometric and state-error bounds but make no physical safety, real-perception, calibration, or accepted-policy claim.
